column1: # TRAIT AUDIT — does the trait/excess/inverse triple intersect all three of its axes?
# A triple is authored, not derived, but it has to read as a plausible collision of the
# bean, the flavour and the form. Nothing checked that until this file. Diagnostic only:
# nothing here rewrites anything. Sheets and the report: `node scripts/trait-audit.mjs`.
#   b / f / m   bean, flavour, form — 0-3 each
#   min         the headline. A sum hides the real failure: a fine trait that ignores
#               one axis completely. A triple is only as good as its weakest axis.
#   note        which axis is weakest, and why
#   3  load-bearing. Take the axis away and the trait stops making sense.
#   2  present and consistent, but would survive a swap to one neighbour on this axis.
#   1  compatible but generic — several values on this axis would serve equally.
#   0  absent, or contradicted: the trait belongs to a different value on the axis.
#   EXCESS — the same quality overdone. Not a different vice, not the trait plus an
#   intensifier. Test: does it still describe someone doing the trait, past the point
#   INVERSE — a disposition someone could hold and defend, not the trait's absence.
#   Test: could facetLeast be written as a person choosing it, with its own freedom
# SCORED COMPARATIVELY, NEVER ONE ENTRY AT A TIME. An absolute judgement on a single
# adjective is noise — any word can be argued into any cell. Each score comes from a
# reading that holds two axes fixed and varies the third: 30 column readings (12 beans,
# one preparation) for b, 12 grid readings (one bean's 5x6) for f and m.
# NO STRUCTURAL SIGNAL SCORES ANYTHING HERE. Against the 21.9% base approved rate,
# "trait lifted verbatim from a parent's list" is 30% approved and "over-/self- excess"
# is 40% — both fire MORE on approved. Bare-negation inverse is 17%, shared stem 21%.
# They print as context on the sheets and stay out of the score. Anchor 4 below is a
# ============ THE ANCHORS — what a 3 looks like, taken from approved entries ============
# Approval is the spec. These eleven were read first and the scale was set to them, so a
# draft scoring 1 means "unlike these", not "unlike a rule I invented". Spread over all
#     FACETS.md's own worked example. Navy stores well and never fails; spicy is heat
#     demanding your whole attention; dried alone among the forms UNDERGOES NOTHING.
#     Tough is heat taken with no visible change — remove any axis and it collapses.
#     Excess: toughness past its use, not a new vice. Inverse: skittish is a person.
#     Same bean, same flavour, form swapped, and the trait moves — which is the whole
#     test. THE FORM IS LOAD-BEARING BY CONTRAST, not agreement: boiled is immersion,
#     where everything softens, and rigid is what navy does in that pot instead. A 3
#     does not require the trait to agree with its axis, only to need it. (The inverse
#     is boiled's own positiveTrait — the form's virtue is what refusing it costs.)
#     Three-way agreement, each irreplaceable: cannellini is "the refusal of the
#     unnecessary", dried takes away "only what is inessential", bitter is the flavour
#     children reject and cultivated palates seek. Ascetic is all three at once.
#     Lifted verbatim from the bean's list and still a 3/3/3, which is why the verbatim
#     check scores nothing. The bean file's own line is that a chickpea "holds its shape
#     in a slow braise or dissolves into something entirely new" — the braise IS boiled,
#     and umami is the slowness that gives it time to choose. Excess "shapeless" is the
#     adapting continued past the point of having a self.
#     Cannellini is exacting; sour is incisive. The form is what makes it cost something:
#     "oil offers no second attempt". Meticulous under fried is care that has to be right
#     the first time, which is a different creature from meticulous under boiled.
#     The second verbatim lift (from the form) that is still a 3. Edamame "reaches
#     conclusions while others are still framing the question"; fried is "the doing is
#     the thinking"; bitter is what makes it cold rather than eager. Excess "peremptory"
#     keeps the quality and removes the room for anyone else.
#     Roasted develops outward "where everyone can see"; umami is depth arrived at
#     slowly; adzuki convenes. Warm is the convening turned outward and left to deepen.
#     Excess is the good test: presumptuous is warmth that has stopped asking, not a
#     Anchors the flavour as TEMPER. Smoked supplies the haze; butter supplies the lack
#     of hurry; sweet is the only reason it is comfortable instead of sinister — the
#     same cell under bitter is eerie (bitter-smoked-green), and it is the flavour alone
#     Smoked's own line is that what a smoked bean says "surfaces in the listener's mind
#     hours later"; edamame sees what is there and skips the preamble; umami is the
#     depth that makes it earned rather than lucky.
#     Kidney protects and stands between; roasted does it in the open; sweet makes it
#     affection rather than guard duty. Excess "possessive" is the bean's own shadow
#     reached by continuing the trait, which is exactly the relation excess should have.
#     Fermented is transformation from within, in conditions no one sees; pinto turns
#     "the swirling interior landscape into something others can touch"; bitter is the
#     acquired taste that stops it being merely expressive. Excess "precious" is the
#     interior work valued past what it made.
